top_categories.workout_context: 310 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
555 Corsica's Corsican secondary roads, Approximately 100 km of forest forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 310 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic 555 Corsica's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At 555 Corsica, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
32,808ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
106ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
310 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 32,808ft of climbing on self-supported Corsican gravel ultra does to your power file on race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 310 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
32,808ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of 555 Corsica. Train it until it feels boring.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At 555 Corsica, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 310 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 310 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at 555 Corsica requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on self-supported corsican gravel ultra to build confidence. Expect: corsican secondary roads, approximately 100 km of forest tracks, self-supported island crossing.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Gravel Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 310 miles of self-supported corsican gravel ultra in Porto-Vecchio to Biguglia, Corsica, France.
